clue.text: Room for a short dictionary

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so the final letter of the named reference work goes

parts.note: Chambers is a well-known British dictionary publisher

explanation.surface: Someone needs space to house a compact dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers Dictionary is the reference many British crossword setters use; dropping its final S leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is an old or formal word for a room, especially a bedroom or hall.

clue.text: Camilla's first husband is getting fat

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
hubby is informal for husband

explanation.surface: Gossip about Camilla's former spouse putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camilla's first husband' suggests Andrew Parker Bowles, but 'first' only takes her initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means plump or rounded, a gentle informal synonym for being overweight.

clue.text: Current yearly numbers thrown out by court

indicators.note: thrown out by says some letters are expelled and something else takes their place

parts.note: annual means happening every year
N is short for number, so two of them
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A judge rejects this year's financial figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the two Ns from ANNUAL and put CT in their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Actual can mean existing at present, as in the actual situation, a sense matching current.

clue.text: It's not easy to disentangle way of getting a druid's photo

indicators.note: the phrase introduces a method, and the method itself is the instruction to split apart the words that follow

parts.note: the method named by the first half of the answer: break the next phrase and take UP out of it
taken as written, the letters to be broken up

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how hard it is to snap a druid's picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the song title and also an instruction: take UP out of A DRUID'S PHOTO and rearrange the rest to get IS HARD TO DO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neil Sedaka song title says separating from a partner is difficult, which the clue phrases as hard to disentangle.

clue.text: Saddo starting out gag

indicators.note: with its start put out, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a saddo is a pitiful person, a wretch

explanation.surface: A sad case begins telling a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inept person.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to make the throat movements of vomiting, which is exactly what retching describes.

clue.text: 'O for a cruiser', praying?

definitions.note: noun answer for a verb-form clue word; the question mark flags the loose fit

indicators.note: the phrase literally instructs us to put one letter in place of another letter inside the next word

parts.note: a cruiser is a kind of naval fighting vessel

explanation.surface: It reads like the opening of a hymn, a plea for a cruiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A of WARSHIP for an O. The quotation marks make the start look like a line of verse, 'O for a thousand tongues'.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is reverent devotion to a god, of which praying is the commonest act, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I'm leaving you as one egg may have said to another

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what someone ending a relationship says

definitions.text: as one egg may have said to another
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: fried eggs flipped and cooked on both sides are served over

explanation.walkthrough: Eggs 'over easy' are fried and turned, so two such eggs could say this of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase announces that a relationship has ended, while fried eggs that have been flipped are described as over.

clue.text: Look up 'spindle'

indicators.note: in a down entry up means reading from the bottom to the top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to leer is to look lecherously

explanation.surface: An instruction to consult a dictionary under a spinning term.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a cylinder on which thread or line is wound, much like a spindle or bobbin.

clue.text: Celebrated from Memphis to Richmond

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Something famous along a route through the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic describes something famous or important in history, so celebrated is a close adjective synonym.

clue.text: Copy partner hugging Matilda in Berlin's artistic mix

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap arms around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: copy and paste go together as a pair of editing commands
the setter Matilda would say I, which is ich in German

explanation.surface: A companion embraces the setter in the German capital's art scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I, and in Berlin I is the German ich; PASTE wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating or blending the styles of other artists, a medley of borrowed elements.

clue.text: Free get together when it's back

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the two-letter word it inside the previous word is read the other way

parts.note: to unite is to join or come together

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet up for nothing, once something has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside UNITE sits the word IT; turn just that pair round to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot or captive is to release it, so free works as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Retro art lines needed to make crosses

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the short word after it is turned round

parts.note: art turned round
lines of poetry are verses

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned artwork and poetry are required to produce cross shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across, so crosses as a verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wool hoarder's disgrace

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: a dark-fleeced animal that keeps its wool on its back
second meaning: the family member who brings shame on the rest

explanation.walkthrough: A sheep 'hoards' wool in the sense that it grows and carries it; the second meaning is the idiom for a shameful relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an embarrassing outcast of a group, while literally it is a dark woolly farm animal.

clue.text: Points provided to cover firm on the rebound

indicators.note: a rebounding ball comes back the way it went, so the combined letters are read backwards
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: provided that means if
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A romantic aside: conditions apply to protecting a business after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' sounds like romance, but it turns the whole assembled group round, not just one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci is the plural of focus, and focal points are centres where attention or rays meet.

clue.text: Where intelligence is drab and less shiny?

parts.note: grey means dull and colourless
matt means not glossy, so more matt is less shiny

explanation.surface: A wry remark that clever people are dull and unpolished.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER is read as the comparative of matt, a dull, non-glossy finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey matter is the brain tissue, and informally the brain itself, seat of thought and cleverness.

clue.text: Vials with nitrogen cleared to be mixed with hair cosmetic

indicators.note: given permission to be mixed, the letters are free to be stirred into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
nitrogen gas exists as two-atom molecules, N2, so it supplies a pair of Ns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lab glassware filled with gas is approved for blending with hair to make a beauty product.
explanation.walkthrough: Nitrogen as a gas is N2, a doubled letter, which supplies both Ns the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail varnish is a lacquer painted on fingernails, one of the commonest cosmetic products.

clue.text: On a criminal trial, one politician is not taking sides

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters next to it are bent out of shape

parts.note: Member of Parliament
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician sitting in judgement on a criminal case remains neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'On' puts I and MP above the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means treating all parties equally, without bias, so neutral and siding with nobody.

clue.text: Hands in hat containing suitable drivel

indicators.note: in puts one group of letters inside another

parts.note: a cap is a hat

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds another within it

parts.note: left and right hands, L and R
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone's hands are in a hat that holds something appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands gives two letters, for left and right, and they act as the outer pair around the word for suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, empty talk, so it means the same as drivel.

clue.text: Most importantly, lover must discard clothing during a dance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: removing clothes strips the outside, so only the inner letters of the word stay

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A racy instruction for a romantic partner to undress at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripped word sits inside BALL, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all is an idiom meaning more than anything else, the same as most importantly.

clue.text: Where to test the UK's standard vacuous Tory politicians

parts.note: a laboratory, where experiments are run
from a British setter's viewpoint, the UK's means our
par is the normal or standard level

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word after it loses its inside and keeps only its two ends

parts.note: just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at empty-headed Conservative MPs being put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour Party is the Conservatives' main rival in Britain, so the Tory surface is a sly misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party is a British political party, a body of politicians, as a collective noun.

clue.text: See 3
Start to enrol in nurse or doctor's profession

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the following word

parts.note: both look after patients, so either is a carer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Signing up to study medicine or nursing is how a medical working life begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's chosen line of work over a lifetime, the same as an occupation or profession.

clue.text: Apply tar cover sheet, essentially?

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so we keep only the central letter of each preceding word

parts.note: the central letter of a five-letter word
the central letter
the central letter
the central letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying a road surface: spread tar to make a covering sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read normally it describes the job, and the middle letters of its four words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave is to lay a hard surface such as asphalt or stones over ground, covering it like a sheet.

clue.text: Bombed an airbase by a body of water

indicators.note: something bombed is blown apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military airfield on the coast came under aerial attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A body of water' looks like the whole definition, but its A is the last letter of the fodder; 'by' joins it on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian Sea is the part of the Indian Ocean between Arabia and India, a large stretch of ocean.

clue.text: Spurious rise in public transport?

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, so a word meaning rise is turned round

parts.note: to go up; written upwards in the grid

explanation.surface: A sceptic questioning reports of growing use of buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or not genuine, and spurious means false, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: See 3
About a Boy primarily is not Grant's interpretation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a boy is a son

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A film buff denies that Hugh Grant starred in About a Boy.
explanation.walkthrough: About a Boy is a 2002 film starring Hugh Grant, which makes the clue read as a trivia dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the process of thinking things through, and one's reasoning is a way of construing matters.

clue.text: See 27
To mill about in march exposing a threat to the global environment

definitions.text: a threat to the global environment

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the word that follows

parts.note: a march is a parade

indicators.note: to mill about is to move aimlessly, and here the word tells us the letters before it wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Protesters milling around at a demonstration reveal an environmental danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing rainforest for oil palm plantations drives deforestation, so this commerce is seen as an ecological menace.

clue.text: Zero dirt should come back to suppress breathing difficulty

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the concealed letters are read from right to left
to suppress is to keep something out of sight, so the answer lies concealed in the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run through the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A cleanliness rule: no grime must return, to keep breathing trouble at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read zeRO DIRT Should backwards to find the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridor is the medical term for a harsh, high-pitched sound caused by an obstructed airway.
